title: What training is mandatory for employers in Portugal?
description: Mandatory employer training in Portugal: the Labor Code's 40 hours a year, safety, harassment, anti corruption, AML, cybersecurity and licensed roles.
shortAnswer: As at November 2026, every employer in Portugal must provide each worker with at least 40 hours of continuous training a year under Article 131 of the Labor Code. On top of that baseline, specific laws require occupational safety and health training, a harassment code of conduct, anti corruption and whistleblowing programs for larger employers, anti money laundering training in obliged entities, cybersecurity training under the NIS2 transposition, and certification for licensed roles.
keyTakeaways: Portugal is unusual in setting a general training quantity: at least 40 hours of continuous training per worker per year, with at least 10% of workers trained each year.
Topic specific duties sit on top of the 40 hours, and some of them count toward it: the anti corruption regime says its training hours count as continuous training.
Employers with 50 or more workers face both the anti corruption regime (RGPC) and the whistleblowing law; employers with seven or more workers need a harassment code of good conduct.

Licensed roles carry their own cycles: 35 hours every five years for professional drivers, a refresher on each five year renewal of a private security card, and 30 credits a year for certified accountants.
Directly applicable EU regulations, such as GDPR, DORA and the AI Act, apply alongside Portuguese law, so a Portuguese register needs an EU layer.

sections.heading: How are mandatory training duties set in Portugal?

blocks.text: Mandatory training in Portugal is set at three levels: a general quantity of training owed to every worker under the Labor Code, topic duties in specific Portuguese laws (many of which transpose EU directives), and EU regulations that apply directly without transposition. The labor inspectorate, the Autoridade para as Condições do Trabalho (ACT), enforces the Labor Code and the occupational safety and health law; sector regulators such as Banco de Portugal, the national anti corruption mechanism (MENAC) and the national cybersecurity center (CNCS) enforce the rest.

The general quantity is the distinctive Portuguese feature. Article 131(2) of the Labor Code requires a minimum of 40 hours of continuous training per year for each worker, or proportional hours for fixed term contracts of three months or more ([Labor Code](https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2009-34546475)). The topic is not prescribed, so the employer decides how to use the hours. Most other markets set training duties topic by topic; compare the [European Union hub](/guides/mandatory-workplace-training-in-the-european-union), which shows the EU layer that Portugal transposes.

Several duties depend on headcount. A harassment code of good conduct applies from seven workers; the anti corruption regime and the internal whistleblowing channel apply from 50 workers; an internal occupational safety and health service becomes mandatory at 400 workers per establishment, or 30 workers exposed to high risk activities. The tables below cover every Portuguese regulation page in this library, and the EU instruments that apply in Portugal, as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What does the Labor Code's 40 hour training rule require?

blocks.text: The Labor Code requires at least 40 hours of continuous training per worker per year and at least 10% of workers trained each year. Hours the employer does not provide within two years convert into a training credit the worker can use, and unprovided hours or credit are paid out when the contract ends.

blocks.text: Three mechanics shape how the hours are managed. Article 131(6) lets the training plan advance hours by up to two years or defer them by the same period. Article 132 converts hours not provided within two years into a credit that is paid, counts as service, needs 10 days' notice and lapses after three years. Article 134 requires payment for unprovided hours or credit on termination. Breaching Article 131(1), (2) or (5) is a grave offense (Article 131(10)). The 40 hour minimum dates from Law 93/2019; the original 2009 text set 35 hours.

blocks.title: Topic duties can count toward the 40 hours
blocks.text: The anti corruption regime states that the hours of its internal training count as continuous training ([Decree-Law 109-E/2021, RGPC Article 9](https://menac.pt/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Dec_Lei-109-E_2021.pdf)). That provision is explicit only for anti corruption training. For other topic duties, whether hours count toward Article 131 is a question to settle in the training plan and, where needed, with legal advice.

sections.heading: What health and safety training must Portuguese employers provide?

blocks.text: Law 102/2009, which transposes the EU Occupational Safety and Health Framework Directive, requires adequate safety and health training for each worker, ongoing training for designated workers, and trained first aid, firefighting and evacuation staff in sufficient numbers. Employers must also organize an occupational safety and health service staffed by certified technicians.

blocks.text: The annual written consultation is easy to miss. Article 18(1)(d) of Law 102/2009 requires the employer to consult in writing, at least once a year, on the safety and health training program, and a breach is a very serious offense ([Law 102/2009](https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2009-56365341)). The Labor Code also doubles the maximum very serious fines for safety and health breaches (Article 556(1)). ACT certifies the entities that deliver courses for employer representatives, employers and designated workers who run safety activities themselves ([ACT](https://portal.act.gov.pt/Pages/FormacaodesenvolvimentoatividadesST.aspx)).

sections.heading: What harassment, equality and anti corruption training is required?

blocks.text: Employers with seven or more workers must adopt a code of good conduct for preventing harassment, and employers with 50 or more workers must run an anti corruption compliance program that includes a training program, plus an internal whistleblowing channel. Listed and public sector enterprises must also publish annual equality plans, in which training is one assessed dimension.

blocks.text: The anti corruption regime is the most training specific of these. Article 5(1) of the RGPC lists a training program as one of four mandatory compliance elements, alongside a corruption risk prevention plan, a code of conduct and a whistleblowing channel, and Article 9 requires internal training for all managers and workers, with content and frequency reflecting each person's exposure to risk ([RGPC](https://menac.pt/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Dec_Lei-109-E_2021.pdf)). MENAC's Guide 1/2023 suggests an annual training needs survey, induction of 6 to 12 hours and a mix of about 25% behavioral, 25% normative and 50% group work ([MENAC Guide 1/2023](https://menac.pt/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/guia-n1-2023.pdf)). Training is not a separately fined offense under Article 20, but managers and the compliance officer can be personally liable under Article 21(4).

Recent amendments to the decree-law have not touched the training provisions. Decree-Law 70/2025 restructured MENAC and republished the decree-law with RGPC Articles 2, 9 and 20 unchanged, and Law 37/2026 amended MENAC's functions from September 1, 2026 without amending the RGPC annex.

sections.heading: What data protection, cybersecurity and AI training applies in Portugal?

blocks.text: Data protection training rests on the GDPR, which applies directly, and on Law 58/2019, which executes it in Portugal and gives the Data Protection Officer a duty to sensitize users to security incidents. Cybersecurity training is set by Decree-Law 125/2025, which transposes NIS2 and makes management bodies responsible for regular training.

blocks.text: Timing matters for the cybersecurity regime. Decree-Law 125/2025 entered into force 120 days after its December 4, 2025 publication, but Article 10(2) defers Article 27(1) and (2), which contain the cyber hygiene and training measure, until 24 months after the implementing regulations are published ([Decree-Law 125/2025](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2025/12/23400/0000400068.pdf)). The management body duty in Article 25 is not deferred. One of the sanctions available is an order to adopt a training plan within six months (Article 67(c)). For financial entities, DORA rather than NIS2 is the sector specific act, and Decree-Law 125/2025 names Banco de Portugal, CMVM and ASF as the special authorities for it.

sections.heading: What anti money laundering training does Portuguese law require?

blocks.text: Law 83/2017 requires obliged entities to give employees specific, regular training appropriate to their sector, and immediate training to new joiners, with records available to the sectoral authorities. Breaching the training duty is listed as a particularly serious offense.

blocks.text: Penalties make the training duty a board level issue. Article 169-A(jj) of Law 83/2017 lists breach of the Article 55(1) to (4) training duty as a particularly serious offense, with fines for credit and financial institutions ranging from EUR 50,000 to EUR 5,000,000 (Article 170(1)), and Article 171 raises maximums to twice the economic benefit or 10% of annual turnover for some entities ([Law 83/2017](https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/lei/2017-108024643)). From 10 July 2027 the EU Anti Money Laundering Regulation will set the training duty directly in Article 12, so a Portuguese program built today needs to be mapped to both texts.

sections.heading: Which licensed roles carry their own training and CPD requirements?

blocks.text: Licensed roles in Portugal carry training tied to the license itself: initial qualification, then periodic refreshers or annual credits, with loss of the right to practice as the consequence of missing them. The financial services competence regimes come from EU directives transposed into Portuguese law.

blocks.text: The private security regime is the most granular. Ordinance 148/2014 makes refresher training mandatory on card renewal or where the last training was more than five years ago, and sets minimum refresher hours for each specialty, from 10 hours for alarm operators to 60 hours for close protection ([Ordinance 148/2014](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2014/07/13700/0390003909.pdf)). For certified accountants, non compliance with the 30 credit rule prevents practice automatically after the proof deadline ([OCC regulation](https://www.occ.pt/pt-pt/ordem/regulamentos/regulamento-de-formacao-profissional-continua)).

sections.heading: What training applies to food businesses and professional drivers?

blocks.text: Professional truck and bus drivers need a driver qualification certificate (CAM) renewed every five years through 35 hours of periodic training. Food businesses train food handlers under the EU hygiene regulation, which applies directly and is enforced in Portugal through official controls.

blocks.text: The CAM regime is enforced at the roadside. The Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT) oversees it, the GNR and PSP enforce it, and a driver without a valid document faces a fine of EUR 500 to EUR 1,500, reduced to EUR 50 to EUR 150 if the document is shown within five days ([Decree-Law 102-C/2020](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2020/12/23802/0022100257.pdf)). Employers running fleets should track each driver's CAM expiry rather than relying on the five year cycle starting at a common date.

sections.heading: How should a Portuguese employer build a single training register?

blocks.text: Build the register so that every training activity is recorded once and counted twice: against the topic duty it satisfies and against the worker's 40 hour Article 131 balance. That double count is what turns the Labor Code minimum from a separate burden into the container for most other obligations.

items: **Set headcount thresholds first.** Record headcount per legal person and establishment: seven workers triggers the harassment code, 50 triggers the RGPC and the whistleblowing channel, and 400 per establishment (or 30 in high risk activities) triggers an internal OSH service.

**List topic duties and their source.** Use the tables above, marking which are Portuguese law, which are EU regulations applying directly, and which are guidance (CITE's model code, MENAC guides, CNPD's Diretriz).

**Track the 40 hours per worker.** Record hours by worker and year, the share of workers trained (at least 10%), any advance or deferral agreed in the training plan, and unprovided hours that are becoming a credit under Article 132.
**Record license cycles per person.** CAM expiry, PSP card expiry, OCC credits by year, and OSH technician CPD over five years all run on individual dates.

**Apply the longest retention rule.** AML training records are kept seven years under Law 83/2017; OSH service documentation and the whistleblowing register five years. See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).
**Hold the annual consultation.** Schedule the written consultation on the safety and health training program required at least once a year by Law 102/2009 and file the record.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each learning outcome to the Portuguese and EU sources it satisfies, so one activity can evidence a topic duty and the Article 131 hours at the same time. When a source changes, such as the AML Regulation replacing parts of Law 83/2017 in 2027, the affected outcomes are identified directly. The [knowledge governance](/platform/knowledge-governance) page describes this.

faqs.q: Do the 40 training hours have to cover specific topics?
faqs.a: No. Article 131 of the Labor Code sets a minimum quantity, 40 hours per worker per year, without prescribing topics. The employer chooses the content in its training plan. Topic duties such as anti corruption or safety training sit alongside it, and the anti corruption regime states expressly that its training hours count as continuous training.

faqs.q: What happens if an employer does not provide the 40 hours?
faqs.a: Breaching Article 131(1), (2) or (5) is a grave offense. Hours not provided within two years also convert into a training credit the worker can use with 10 days' notice, which is paid and counts as service, and unprovided hours or credit must be paid on termination of the contract.

faqs.q: Does a small company in Portugal need anti corruption or whistleblowing training?
faqs.a: The anti corruption regime and the whistleblowing channel duty apply to legal persons with 50 or more workers, although the whistleblowing law also covers entities in its annex regardless of size. A company with seven or more workers still needs a harassment code of good conduct, and every employer owes safety training and the 40 hours.

faqs.q: Do EU regulations add training duties in Portugal?
faqs.a: Yes. Regulations such as the GDPR, DORA and the AI Act apply directly in Portugal without transposition, and the EU Anti Money Laundering Regulation will apply from 10 July 2027. Directives such as NIS2 and the Whistleblower Directive reach employers through Portuguese laws, for example Decree-Law 125/2025 and Law 93/2021.
